title: gpu oom + driver/library mismatch scratchpad
content:
Notes to self / incident breadcrumbs - GPU OOM + driver/library mismatch

Context:
- Running inference service (gpt-neoX-20B variant) on Dedicated cluster (p4d-like nodes).
- Symptoms: intermittent CUDA OOM when batch_size=1 on long sequences (~4k tokens) for a specific model variant. Some pods show fatal driver/library mismatch at start: 'Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch' or container-level 'CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device'.
- Reproducible on node gpu-node-17 but not gpu-node-03. Suspect driver mismatch / leftover drivers after node upgrade or mixed CUDA runtimes in container images.

What I saw (commands + outputs):
- On host:
  $ nvidia-smi
  Fri May 10 12:11:09 2024
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 470.199.02    Driver Version: 470.199.02    CUDA Version: 11.4   |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
  0    A100-SXM4-40G     Off  | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                     0 |

- Inside container (fail case):
  $ docker run --gpus all --rm --runtime=nvidia --entrypoint /bin/bash my-infer-image -c "nvidia-smi"
  NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver. Make sure that the latest NVIDIA driver is installed and running.

  # trying quick checks inside container
  $ ls -l /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so*
  lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 14 May 10 10:00 /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so -> libcudart.so.11.0
  -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 1830200 Apr  2  2024 /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0

  $ python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
  11.7
  True

  # but when importing model:
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/opt/app/serve/infer.py", line 42, in <module>
      model = load_model('redwood/gpt-neox-20b-quant')
    File "/opt/app/serve/model_loader.py", line 110, in load_model
      torch.cuda.init()
  RuntimeError: CUDA error: driver/library version mismatch

- On some nodes got OOM logs during token generation:
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 39.66 GiB total capacity; 36.12 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free, 1.28 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  Suggested steps: reduce batch size, reduce sequence length, enable gradient checkpointing (N/A for inference), call torch.cuda.empty_cache() between requests.

Commands/troubleshooting I tried (chronological):
1) Confirm host driver vs container CUDA:
   - On host: nvidia-smi -> Driver 470.199.02 (CUDA 11.4)
   - In container: nvcc --version shows CUDA 11.7 (toolkit baked into image) and torch reports CUDA version 11.7.
   Conclusion: container built with newer CUDA toolkit than host driver -> possible driver/library mismatch.

2) Recreated container with nvidia-container-runtime v3, tried with --gpus all and with --runtime=nvidia to see diff: same error.

3) Verified /proc/driver/nvidia/version on host and inside container (mounted /proc): host shows 470.199.02, inside container accessible via mount shows same file but error persists; likely because libcuda available mismatch for containerized libs.

4) Checked symlinks: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.470.199.02; inside container the libcuda.so is not present or is a mismatched version.

5) Workaround test: launched container without shipping CUDA toolkit in image (use minimal base that relies on host's /usr/local/cuda and libcuda). This made python torch.cuda.is_available() return False in that image — likely because wheel was built against 11.7 and host driver supports 11.4.

6) Tried downgrading torch to a wheel built for CUDA 11.4 (pip install torch==1.12.1+cu11.4) in a test image — after redeploy, the driver/library mismatch disappeared, but now inference frequently OOMs earlier. Could be due to different memory allocator behavior across versions.

7) Node-level checks: kernel logs show occasional 'GPU hung' and 'Resetting GPU' messages during heavy inference. dmesg snippets:
   NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
   NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:00:1e: GPU has fallen off the bus.

8) Model/config mitigations tried: reduce batch_size 1 -> 0.5 (micro-batching), reduce max_seq_len from 4096 to 2048, enable kv cache offload to CPU for past tokens (experiment). All reduced OOM frequency but didn't eliminate driver/init errors.

Hypotheses / root cause candidates:
- Driver/toolkit mismatch: container CUDA (11.7) vs host driver (470.x for CUDA11.4) -> leads to 'driver/library mismatch' on some nodes. Some nodes upgraded partially causing mixed environments.
- Corrupted / mismatched libcuda.so or LD_LIBRARY_PATH exposing wrong libraries inside container (e.g., image ships libcuda from build time).
- Node hardware/firmware issue (GPU falling off the bus) causing driver reset then subsequent containers fail with NVML errors until node reboot.
- MIG or multi-tenant noise: other tenants exhausting GPU memory or using exclusive processes causing OOM for our pods.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Short term (hotfix): pin runtime to torch wheel built for host driver CUDA version (11.4) for affected model variant and redeploy on nodes showing mismatch. Roll back to previously stable image if available.
- Mid term: standardize on compatibility matrix in infra: container CUDA toolkit vs host driver mapping. Add pre-deploy check that compares host driver (nvidia-smi --query) to image-reported torch.version.cuda / nvcc --version. CI job to fail if mismatch.
- Node remediation: schedule cordon/drain + reboot on gpu-node-17, re-run full nvidia-driver reinstall, check firmware.
- Observability: add a startup probe to model pods that runs a quick torch.cuda.init() + simple CUDA kernel to surface driver/library mismatch before accepting traffic; emit structured telemetry to Console (metric: gpu.init_errors with tags driver_mismatch / nvml_error / oom).
- Long term: build images per driver family (11.4, 11.7, 12.x) and use node labels + admission Webhook to ensure image -> node compatibility.

Notes for follow-ups / potential gotchas:
- On some kernels, torch reports cuda version 11.7 but will work with driver 470.x for many operations; mismatch errors surface only for certain API calls (NVML, JIT kernels). Edge-case race between driver reset and container start can expose 'driver/library mismatch'.
- Check for leftover nvidia-container-toolkit or old nvidia runtime remnants on hosts after driver upgrade.
- libnvidia-ml.so path precedence matters; mounting host /usr/lib/nvidia or /usr/local/cuda into container can help, but be careful with distro lib paths.

Relevant links / tickets: SERV-1289 (investigating driver mismatch), PR #412 (small patch to image build to align cuda toolkit), slack thread: #infra-gpus May 10 thread.

Scratch commands to re-run quickly:
- host: sudo apt list --installed | grep nvidia-driver
- host: sudo dpkg -l | grep nvidia
- container: python -c "import ctypes; print(ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so').nvmlInit())"  # quick NVML check (wrap try/except)
- container: ldd $(python -c 'import torchvision; print(torchvision.__file__)') | grep cuda
- check memory: watch -n1 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used --format=csv

If I can't resolve quickly: escalate to infra SRE (Maya) and schedule node maintenance window.

Personal notes: keep this doc as scratchpad until we have final postmortem. Clean up and move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/incidents when we finalize.

-- Arya
